text: Every single person who signs into the Power BI service holds one of three license types — and what you can actually do with that license depends on more than just which one you happen to have.

Free lets you build reports and dashboards for yourself, and genuinely nothing more than that — no sharing, no collaboration with anyone else at all. Pro adds real sharing and collaboration, but only with other Pro users. Premium Per User adds most Premium capacity features on top of Pro, but again, only shareable with other PPU users specifically.

Here's the part almost everybody misses the first time through: a Free-license user can absolutely view shared content, but only if that content happens to live in a workspace assigned to a Premium or Fabric capacity. The license alone never decides this by itself — where the actual workspace lives matters just as much as who's trying to view it.

Microsoft Fabric is the umbrella platform that now houses Power BI alongside data engineering, data science, and real-time analytics tools, all sharing one underlying capacity and one storage layer. A Fabric F64 or larger capacity does everything a Power BI Premium capacity used to do, plus unlocks Fabric's other workloads on top of that.

You don't need to buy anything at all to follow along with this course — a Microsoft 365 subscription, an admin-assigned license, or a free Fabric capacity trial all work fine. Once you actually know what your license allows you to do, Lesson 69 puts you inside your very first real workspace.
